Champ Select Basics: Bans, Picks and Roles

How champion select works in ranked, what to ban, when to pick safe champions, and what to do when things go wrong before the game even starts.

How champ select works

Before every ranked game you go through champion select ("champ select" or "draft"). Your role is assigned before it starts, based on the two positions you queued for. Then it runs in three parts:

  1. Ban phase. Each player bans one champion, so up to 10 champions are removed from the game. Bans are revealed together at the end of the phase.
  2. Pick phase. Teams take turns locking in champions in a 1-2-2-2-2-1 order: the blue side picks first, then red picks two, blue picks two, and so on, until red makes the last pick.
  3. Final phase. A short window to set your runes, summoner spells and skin, and to trade champions with a teammate if you both agree.

The order matters. The first picks have to choose without knowing much about the enemy team. The last picks get to see almost everything and can react to it.

What to ban

You only get one ban, so use it on purpose. Good reasons to ban a champion:

  • It counters your main. If you play Veigar and always struggle against Katarina, banning her protects your pick.
  • You hate playing against it. A champion you don't understand will beat you more often than its win rate suggests.
  • It's very strong this patch. Check the tier list for champions that are overperforming.
Common mistakeNever ban the champion a teammate is hovering. It's the fastest way to start the game with an angry teammate. Look at your team's hovers before you lock in your ban.

Blind pick vs counter pick

A blind pick is choosing your champion before you know who you'll be laning against. A counter pick is choosing after you've seen your opponent, so you can pick something that beats them.

If you pick early, choose a champion that's safe against most opponents: one with range, an escape, or few bad matchups. In mid, Ahri and Malzahar are classic safe picks. In bot, long-range marksmen like Caitlyn and Jhin rarely get bullied out of lane.

If you pick late, you can look at your lane opponent and pick into them. You don't have to: a champion you know well is usually a better choice than a 'counter' you've barely played. The Counter-Picking: When and How to Pick Into Someone guide goes deeper.

Bot lane has an extra layer: the ADC and support pick as a pair. If your support picks first, they should choose something flexible, like a tank who works with most marksmen, and let the ADC react to the enemy bot lane. If you really want to counter pick but you're picking early, you can ask a later teammate to swap pick order with you. Many players are happy to help if you ask nicely.

Hover early and talk to your team

Hovering means selecting a champion without locking it in. Your teammates can see your hover, so hover your intended pick as early as you can. It helps them plan bans and picks around you.

Short, friendly messages go a long way:

  • "I'll play Ahri, ban Katarina pls?"
  • "Can someone pick a tank? I can play Malzahar or Lux."
  • "Last pick, what do we need?"
Pro tipIf you pick early, say which champions you're comfortable on. A late-picking teammate can then counter the enemy for you or fill a gap in the team.

When someone takes your role

Sometimes a teammate asks for your role, or picks a champion for your lane. Stay calm: arguing in champ select almost always ends in a loss.

  • Ask politely which role they were assigned. Often it's a simple misunderstanding.
  • If you can play their role, a swap is fine. Remember that role quests come from your assigned position, so only trade roles if you both really want to.
  • If they refuse and you can't play anything else, pick the safest champion you have and play for the team.

Never respond by picking a champion just to 'troll' them. Two players ruining the game is worse than one.

Build a small champion pool

You don't need to know 50 champions. A small pool for your main role is enough to climb:

  • One safe blind pick you can play into anything (for example Ahri mid or Caitlyn bot).
  • One or two champions for specific situations, like Malzahar into assassins, or Ziggs when your team needs poke and turret pressure.
  • Something for your secondary role, in case you get it.

Practice your picks in different situations with the Draft Practice tool.

Should you dodge?

Leaving champ select ("dodging") costs you some LP and makes you wait before you can queue again, and the penalty grows if you dodge repeatedly. Only dodge when a game is clearly lost before it starts: a teammate who says they'll throw the game on purpose, or a team with no chance to work together. Don't dodge just because you got your second role or a teammate picked something you don't like.

Key takeaways

  • Ranked picks go 1-2-2-2-2-1. Early picks blind pick, late picks can counter pick.
  • Ban what counters your main or what you don't understand, never a teammate's hover.
  • Pick safe champions when you pick early, and a comfortable champion beats an unfamiliar counter.
  • Hover early and tell your team what you can play.
  • A small pool (a safe blind pick plus one or two situational picks) is enough to climb.
